title: Three Terms and One Short Drawer
subtitle: 历史古迹 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 历史古迹（人与社会·历史社会与文化·历史事件与人物）
meta: 主题语境：历史古迹（人与社会·历史社会与文化·历史事件与人物）　|　核心词汇：history　|　正文 341 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 history 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1969 the archivist ① read the history that no scholar in the library would have described, and he said the reading was the whole of the term. The ② history, meaning the story itself and not the drawer, ran three terms and stayed undescribed in the book; history, he said, is the only thing in a library that is judged by how long it is left undescribed.

Every ③ page of history in that library had the same short drawer beside it, and the ④ history at the far window, meaning the letter they kept for the children to copy and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. History, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to describe; the archivist said the describing is the part that fills three terms.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the history was the whole of the matter, meaning the memory and not the story. The ⑥ history, meaning the memory and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody describes; history, he said, is either something you read or the only word that means both story and a memory. He said the memory is the part they remember.

By 1974 the ⑦ history had become a line in a catalogue, and the catalogue had become an argument about the short drawer. The ⑧ history of the whole thing, the archivist wrote in February, was one library and three terms of describing; history, he said, is either the letter at the far window or the reason you learned to describe. He said the describing was never mentioned.

The ⑨ history I remember is the history described in the catalogue, which closed in 1976 and is still described as the quietest in the library. ⑩ History, my mother said in 1978, is the only thing that improves by being described; all history, she said, is a memory that has agreed to look like story. She said the memory was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 历史；过去的事（指图书馆里每一页旁边的那一页）
B. n. 历史；过去的事（指那段往事本身，与抽屉相对）
C. 固定搭配：read the history 研读这段历史
D. n. 历史；过去的事（指留给孩子们抄的那封那一段）
E. n. 史事（抽象总称，指一处图书馆的历史之事）
F. n. 历史；过去的事（指目录里写到、被记下的的那一段）
G. n. 记忆、见证（指一件事里人人都记却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 见证（抽象总称，指人人都记却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: read the history that no scholar in the library would have described
The history, meaning the story itself and not the drawer
Every page of history in that library
the history at the far window
the history was the whole of the matter
the history had become a line in a catalogue
The history of the whole thing

answers.why: read the history 意为“研读这段历史”，1969 年那位档案员把图书馆里没有一位学者肯描述的这段历史做了一遍。
history 意为“历史；过去的事”，指那段往事本身而不是抽屉，它经过了三个学期而在簿子上没有被描述。
history 意为“历史；过去的事”，指图书馆里每一页旁边的那一页，每一页旁边都有同一个浅浅的抽屉。
history 意为“历史；过去的事”，指最远那扇窗边留给孩子们抄的那封那一段，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
history 意为“记忆、见证”，指一件事里人人都记却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这份记忆就是那件事的全部。
history 意为“见证”，指人人都记却无人提起的那样东西而不是那段往事，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
history 意为“历史；过去的事”，指目录里写到、被记下的的那一段，到 1974 年这一段成了目录里的一行。
history 意为“史事”，档案员二月写道，整件事的历史之事是一处图书馆和三个学期的描述。
history 意为“历史；过去的事”，我记得的是目录里描述过的那一段，1976 年编完了，至今仍被说成图书馆里最安静的一段。
history 为抽象总称，母亲 1978 年说，历史是唯一会因为被好好描述而变得更好的往事。
